punchline: A school programme taught that processed food contains no water, and a columnist read the manual.
thirty_sec: Brain Gym was used in at least hundreds of British state schools. Ben Goldacre got hold of the teachers' manual and wrote in the Guardian that it taught that processed foods contain no water and that rocking your head sends blood to your frontal lobes. He said exercise breaks are fine; his target was the invented science attached to them. Angry teachers wrote in. He replied that he didn't need to visit a classroom to find out whether processed food contains water.
